UX_VIS_PAGINATIONVS_001.quote: Endless scrolling is not recommended for goal-oriented finding tasks, such as those requiring people to locate specific content or compare options.

UX_VIS_PROXWHITES_001.title: Proximity Grouping via Whitespace
UX_VIS_PROXWHITES_001.rule: Ensure the whitespace between distinct UI groups is noticeably larger than the whitespace within a group to clearly communicate relationships and visual hierarchy.
UX_VIS_PROXWHITES_001.detect: Measure spacing tokens or CSS margins/padding. The gap between related elements (e.g., a label and its input, or a heading and its paragraph) must be strictly smaller than the gap separating that group from the next adjacent group.
UX_VIS_PROXWHITES_001.when_to_apply: When designing forms, navigation menus, text layouts, and responsive grids to help task-focused users quickly scan and identify related elements.
UX_VIS_PROXWHITES_001.when_not_to_apply: When elements are already strongly grouped using explicit visual boundaries (like borders or distinct background colors - Gestalt Common Region), though proximity still reinforces these boundaries.
UX_VIS_PROXWHITES_001.quote: Using varying amounts of whitespace to either unite or separate elements is key to communicating meaningful groupings.

UX_VIS_FZPATTERN_001.title: Align CTAs with Natural Reading Patterns (F/Z-Patterns)
UX_VIS_FZPATTERN_001.rule: Leverage natural reading patterns (F-pattern, Z-pattern) for text-heavy layouts, and place interactive elements (like CTAs) at the end of the user's compositional flow to prevent visual backtracking.
UX_VIS_FZPATTERN_001.detect: Identify text-heavy pages or forms. Check if the primary CTA (e.g., 'Submit' or 'Buy Now') is placed before the information required to make the decision or complete the action, forcing the user's eye to move backwards.
UX_VIS_FZPATTERN_001.when_to_apply: Apply to text-heavy pages, search results, and sequential forms where users scan in predictable F or Z patterns.
UX_VIS_FZPATTERN_001.when_not_to_apply: Do not rely solely on these patterns when a page uses strong visual hierarchy, graphics, and rhythm to intentionally create a custom compositional flow.
UX_VIS_FZPATTERN_001.quote: On a text-heavy and graphic-light page, a visitor’s eye likely follows something like a Z-pattern or F-pattern... it makes sense to place the button to search after the form field, because the natural process is to fill in the field and then click the button.

UX_PRD_BMAPDIAGN_001.title: Diagnose Onboarding CTAs using B=MAP
UX_PRD_BMAPDIAGN_001.rule: Ensure every critical onboarding CTA simultaneously provides Motivation, Ability, and a Prompt. If a user fails to act, diagnose the drop-off by identifying which of these three elements is missing.
UX_PRD_BMAPDIAGN_001.detect: Audit onboarding drop-off points. Check if the user knows why to act (Motivation), how to act easily (Ability), and is explicitly asked to act now (Prompt).
UX_PRD_BMAPDIAGN_001.when_to_apply: When designing or optimizing user onboarding flows, permission requests, or core activation events where user action is required.
UX_PRD_BMAPDIAGN_001.when_not_to_apply: When actions are automated by the system or when dealing with passive informational consumption rather than interactive tasks.
UX_PRD_BMAPDIAGN_001.quote: Behavior happens when Motivation, Ability, and a Prompt come together at the same time. When a behavior does not occur, at least one of those three elements is missing.

UX_TMP_POGRAPHY_001.title: Prefer Left-Aligned Text for Paragraphs
UX_TMP_POGRAPHY_001.rule: Use left-aligned text for multi-line paragraphs to optimize readability and scannability.
UX_TMP_POGRAPHY_001.detect:
Identify text blocks with `text-align: center`, `text-align: right`, or `text-align: justify` applied to multi-line `

` elements or text containers.
UX_TMP_POGRAPHY_001.when_to_apply: When styling body copy, articles, descriptions, and multi-line text blocks in LTR (left-to-right) languages.
UX_TMP_POGRAPHY_001.when_not_to_apply: Short titles, single-line UI elements, data table numbers (which should be right-aligned), or when designing for RTL (right-to-left) languages.
UX_TMP_POGRAPHY_001.quote: Body text generally looks nicer and is easier to read when the lines are spaced apart. The recommended line height is around 1.5 – 2 (double spaced).

UX_TMP_ORD_AUTH_001.title: Allow Password Unmasking with Device-Specific Defaults
UX_TMP_ORD_AUTH_001.rule: Provide a toggle to unmask password inputs during account creation. On desktop, hide the password by default and provide a 'Show password' control. On mobile and tablet devices, show the password by default and provide a 'Hide password' control.
UX_TMP_ORD_AUTH_001.detect: Identify password creation inputs. Verify the presence of a visibility toggle. Check if the default input type is 'password' on desktop and 'text' on mobile.
UX_TMP_ORD_AUTH_001.when_to_apply: When designing password creation or password reset forms where users are generating new, complex strings.
UX_TMP_ORD_AUTH_001.when_not_to_apply: When designing standard login forms for frequently used accounts, or in highly sensitive public environments where shoulder-surfing is a severe threat.
UX_TMP_ORD_AUTH_001.quote: Allow users to unmask the password. Seeing the password will support memory and will allow users to check their work. On desktop, hide the password by default, and next to it, place a checkbox labeled Show password. On mobile devices and tablets, show the password by default and let users toggle the visibility with a Hide password control.

UX_TMP_ILTERING_001.title: Prefer Simple Filters Over Facets for Simple Datasets
UX_TMP_ILTERING_001.rule: Implement simple filters instead of full faceted navigation unless the dataset is extremely large and requires narrowing across multiple distinct dimensions, as facets increase both user interaction cost and system maintenance overhead.
UX_TMP_ILTERING_001.detect: Evaluate the search or data table interface to see if multi-dimensional faceted navigation is used for a small dataset where 1-2 basic filters would suffice.
UX_TMP_ILTERING_001.when_to_apply: Apply when designing data tables or search interfaces for small-to-medium datasets, or when the underlying data lacks comprehensive metadata across multiple dimensions.
UX_TMP_ILTERING_001.when_not_to_apply: Do not apply when dealing with extremely large, complex datasets (e.g., e-commerce catalogs) where users must narrow results by several orthogonal dimensions simultaneously.
UX_TMP_ILTERING_001.quote: The extra power of faceted navigation also adds interaction cost by presenting users with more options to comprehend and manipulate. A simple filter can often be easier to understand and faster to use.

UX_TMP_AN_TABLE_001.title: Use Dynamic Table over Experimental Table
UX_TMP_AN_TABLE_001.rule: Use the `@atlaskit/dynamic-table` component for data tables instead of the experimental `Table` package, which is deprioritized and unsupported for production.
UX_TMP_AN_TABLE_001.when_to_apply: When implementing data tables within the Atlassian Design System ecosystem.
UX_TMP_AN_TABLE_001.when_not_to_apply: When working outside the Atlassian ecosystem.
UX_TMP_AN_TABLE_001.quote: This package was an experiment, and is currently deprioritized. It is not recommended for use in production, and we are not providing support for it at this time. Consider using @atlaskit/dynamic-table instead.

UX_TMP_EX_TABLE_001.title: Right-Align Numeric Table Cells
UX_TMP_EX_TABLE_001.rule: Right-align numeric cells and their corresponding column titles in index tables.
UX_TMP_EX_TABLE_001.detect: Identify columns containing numeric data (e.g., totals, counts) and verify that both the header and cell contents have right alignment applied.
UX_TMP_EX_TABLE_001.when_to_apply: When displaying numeric data such as currency, quantities, or measurements in a data table.
UX_TMP_EX_TABLE_001.when_not_to_apply: When numbers are used as identifiers (e.g., order IDs, phone numbers) where mathematical comparison is irrelevant.
UX_TMP_EX_TABLE_001.quote: Numeric cells and titles should be right aligned with the Text component

UX_TMP_D_MOTION_001.title: Respect prefers-reduced-motion for vestibular accessibility
UX_TMP_D_MOTION_001.rule: Use the `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` CSS media query to remove, reduce, or replace non-essential motion-based animations (such as scaling or panning large objects) with safer alternatives like opacity fades.
UX_TMP_D_MOTION_001.detect: Scan CSS for `animation` or `transition` properties—especially those using `transform: scale()` or `transform: translate()`—and verify they are overridden or disabled within a `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` block.
UX_TMP_D_MOTION_001.when_to_apply: Whenever implementing non-essential animations, transitions, or auto-playing videos, particularly those that move or scale large areas of the screen.
UX_TMP_D_MOTION_001.when_not_to_apply: When the motion is strictly essential to the core functionality of the application, or if the animation is already a safe, non-triggering effect (like a simple color or opacity change).
UX_TMP_D_MOTION_001.quote: The prefers-reduced-motion CSS media feature is used to detect if a user has enabled a setting on their device to minimize the amount of non-essential motion. The setting is used to convey to the browser on the device that the user prefers an interface that removes, reduces, or replaces motion-based animations.

UX_TMP_NIMATION_001.title: Animation Timing and Distraction Prevention
UX_TMP_NIMATION_001.rule: Trigger cause-and-effect animations within 0.1 seconds of user action to maintain direct manipulation. For non-critical peripheral elements, use slow fade-ins without position shifts to avoid distracting users from their primary task.
UX_TMP_NIMATION_001.detect: Measure delay between user action and animation start (must be < 0.1s). Check peripheral elements for fast sliding motions that interrupt reading patterns.
UX_TMP_NIMATION_001.when_to_apply: Use fast (< 0.1s) animations for direct user interactions and critical alerts. Use slow, stationary fade-ins for contextual, indirectly triggered features.
UX_TMP_NIMATION_001.when_not_to_apply: Do not use fast, sliding animations for non-critical peripheral elements. Avoid lengthy, repetitive animations for frequently accessed elements like main menus.
UX_TMP_NIMATION_001.quote: For an animation to effectively convey a cause-and-effect relationship between UI elements, the effect must begin within 0.1 seconds of the initial user action.

UX_TMP__VISIBLE_001.title: Search Box Visibility and Placement
UX_TMP__VISIBLE_001.rule: Display search as a visible text-input field at the top of the page (preferably the top right or left) rather than hiding it behind a link or icon, and ensure the input field is wide enough to display typical queries without scrolling.
UX_TMP__VISIBLE_001.detect: Check the homepage and complex interior pages for a visible text input field near the top of the page. Verify it is not hidden behind a toggle or link, and check that its width accommodates typical query lengths.
UX_TMP__VISIBLE_001.when_to_apply: Apply to homepages, complex interior pages, and any site where users frequently rely on search to navigate or find specific items.
UX_TMP__VISIBLE_001.when_not_to_apply: Very simple interior pages where a search link or icon might suffice to save space, or sites with extremely minimal content where search is unnecessary.
UX_TMP__VISIBLE_001.quote: On homepages, search should be a type-in field and not a link. Put the search box at the top of the page, usually in the right hand corner... The search input field should be wide enough to contain the typical query

UX_GEN_LEFTALIGNEDT_001.title: Prefer Left-Aligned Text for Paragraphs
UX_GEN_LEFTALIGNEDT_001.rule: Use left-aligned text for multi-line paragraphs to optimize readability and scannability.
UX_GEN_LEFTALIGNEDT_001.detect:
Identify text blocks with `text-align: center`, `text-align: right`, or `text-align: justify` applied to multi-line `

` elements or text containers.
UX_GEN_LEFTALIGNEDT_001.when_to_apply: When styling body copy, articles, descriptions, and multi-line text blocks in LTR (left-to-right) languages.
UX_GEN_LEFTALIGNEDT_001.when_not_to_apply: Short titles, single-line UI elements, data table numbers (which should be right-aligned), or when designing for RTL (right-to-left) languages.
UX_GEN_LEFTALIGNEDT_001.quote: Body text generally looks nicer and is easier to read when the lines are spaced apart. The recommended line height is around 1.5 – 2 (double spaced).

UX_GEN_ANIMATIONTIM_001.title: Animation Timing and Distraction Prevention
UX_GEN_ANIMATIONTIM_001.rule: Trigger cause-and-effect animations within 0.1 seconds of user action to maintain direct manipulation. For non-critical peripheral elements, use slow fade-ins without position shifts to avoid distracting users from their primary task.
UX_GEN_ANIMATIONTIM_001.detect: Measure delay between user action and animation start (must be < 0.1s). Check peripheral elements for fast sliding motions that interrupt reading patterns.
UX_GEN_ANIMATIONTIM_001.when_to_apply: Use fast (< 0.1s) animations for direct user interactions and critical alerts. Use slow, stationary fade-ins for contextual, indirectly triggered features.
UX_GEN_ANIMATIONTIM_001.when_not_to_apply: Do not use fast, sliding animations for non-critical peripheral elements. Avoid lengthy, repetitive animations for frequently accessed elements like main menus.
UX_GEN_ANIMATIONTIM_001.quote: For an animation to effectively convey a cause-and-effect relationship between UI elements, the effect must begin within 0.1 seconds of the initial user action.

UX_GEN_PREFERSREDUC_001.title: Respect prefers-reduced-motion for vestibular accessibility
UX_GEN_PREFERSREDUC_001.rule: Use the `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` CSS media query to remove, reduce, or replace non-essential motion-based animations (such as scaling or panning large objects) with safer alternatives like opacity fades.
UX_GEN_PREFERSREDUC_001.detect: Scan CSS for `animation` or `transition` properties—especially those using `transform: scale()` or `transform: translate()`—and verify they are overridden or disabled within a `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` block.
UX_GEN_PREFERSREDUC_001.when_to_apply: Whenever implementing non-essential animations, transitions, or auto-playing videos, particularly those that move or scale large areas of the screen.
UX_GEN_PREFERSREDUC_001.when_not_to_apply: When the motion is strictly essential to the core functionality of the application, or if the animation is already a safe, non-triggering effect (like a simple color or opacity change).
UX_GEN_PREFERSREDUC_001.quote: The prefers-reduced-motion CSS media feature is used to detect if a user has enabled a setting on their device to minimize the amount of non-essential motion. The setting is used to convey to the browser on the device that the user prefers an interface that removes, reduces, or replaces motion-based animations.

UX_GEN_MATCHFILTERI_001.title: Prefer Simple Filters Over Facets for Simple Datasets
UX_GEN_MATCHFILTERI_001.rule: Implement simple filters instead of full faceted navigation unless the dataset is extremely large and requires narrowing across multiple distinct dimensions, as facets increase both user interaction cost and system maintenance overhead.
UX_GEN_MATCHFILTERI_001.detect: Evaluate the search or data table interface to see if multi-dimensional faceted navigation is used for a small dataset where 1-2 basic filters would suffice.
UX_GEN_MATCHFILTERI_001.when_to_apply: Apply when designing data tables or search interfaces for small-to-medium datasets, or when the underlying data lacks comprehensive metadata across multiple dimensions.
UX_GEN_MATCHFILTERI_001.when_not_to_apply: Do not apply when dealing with extremely large, complex datasets (e.g., e-commerce catalogs) where users must narrow results by several orthogonal dimensions simultaneously.
UX_GEN_MATCHFILTERI_001.quote: The extra power of faceted navigation also adds interaction cost by presenting users with more options to comprehend and manipulate. A simple filter can often be easier to understand and faster to use.

UX_GEN_RIGHTALIGNNU_001.title: Right-Align Numeric Table Cells
UX_GEN_RIGHTALIGNNU_001.rule: Right-align numeric cells and their corresponding column titles in index tables.
UX_GEN_RIGHTALIGNNU_001.detect: Identify columns containing numeric data (e.g., totals, counts) and verify that both the header and cell contents have right alignment applied.
UX_GEN_RIGHTALIGNNU_001.when_to_apply: When displaying numeric data such as currency, quantities, or measurements in a data table.
UX_GEN_RIGHTALIGNNU_001.when_not_to_apply: When numbers are used as identifiers (e.g., order IDs, phone numbers) where mathematical comparison is irrelevant.
UX_GEN_RIGHTALIGNNU_001.quote: Numeric cells and titles should be right aligned with the Text component

UX_GEN_USESTABLETAB_001.title: Use Dynamic Table over Experimental Table
UX_GEN_USESTABLETAB_001.rule: Use the `@atlaskit/dynamic-table` component for data tables instead of the experimental `Table` package, which is deprioritized and unsupported for production.
UX_GEN_USESTABLETAB_001.when_to_apply: When implementing data tables within the Atlassian Design System ecosystem.
UX_GEN_USESTABLETAB_001.when_not_to_apply: When working outside the Atlassian ecosystem.
UX_GEN_USESTABLETAB_001.quote: This package was an experiment, and is currently deprioritized. It is not recommended for use in production, and we are not providing support for it at this time. Consider using @atlaskit/dynamic-table instead.

UX_GEN_VISIBLESEARC_001.title: Search Box Visibility and Placement
UX_GEN_VISIBLESEARC_001.rule: Display search as a visible text-input field at the top of the page (preferably the top right or left) rather than hiding it behind a link or icon, and ensure the input field is wide enough to display typical queries without scrolling.
UX_GEN_VISIBLESEARC_001.detect: Check the homepage and complex interior pages for a visible text input field near the top of the page. Verify it is not hidden behind a toggle or link, and check that its width accommodates typical query lengths.
UX_GEN_VISIBLESEARC_001.when_to_apply: Apply to homepages, complex interior pages, and any site where users frequently rely on search to navigate or find specific items.
UX_GEN_VISIBLESEARC_001.when_not_to_apply: Very simple interior pages where a search link or icon might suffice to save space, or sites with extremely minimal content where search is unnecessary.
UX_GEN_VISIBLESEARC_001.quote: On homepages, search should be a type-in field and not a link. Put the search box at the top of the page, usually in the right hand corner... The search input field should be wide enough to contain the typical query

UX_TMP_IXELMOJO_001.title: Aesthetic Peak-End Optimization
UX_TMP_IXELMOJO_001.rule: Concentrate high-fidelity aesthetic polish on the most intense point of the user journey (the peak) and the final step (the end) to disproportionately improve the overall perception of the experience.
UX_TMP_IXELMOJO_001.detect: Aesthetic effort is spread evenly across all screens, or the final confirmation/success screens are treated as an afterthought with generic styling.
UX_TMP_IXELMOJO_001.when_to_apply: When prioritizing design resources across a complex user flow, such as a checkout process, onboarding sequence, or long-form data entry.
UX_TMP_IXELMOJO_001.when_not_to_apply: When the entire flow is extremely short (e.g., a single-click action) where the whole interaction is essentially the peak and end simultaneously.
UX_TMP_IXELMOJO_001.quote: By creating visually appealing highlights (a delightful animation, a beautiful confirmation screen) and ensuring the final step is seamless, you can leave a lasting positive impression that overshadows any minor frustrations.

UX_TMP_PPLE_HIL_001.title: Translate ML Confidence into Actionable Suggestions
UX_TMP_PPLE_HIL_001.rule: Present machine learning confidence scores as actionable advice or semantic categories rather than raw numerical percentages, unless the domain specifically requires statistical data.
UX_TMP_PPLE_HIL_001.detect: Look for UI elements displaying raw ML probability percentages (e.g., '97% match', '80% confidence') outside of strictly statistical or scientific contexts.
UX_TMP_PPLE_HIL_001.when_to_apply: When presenting predictive results, recommendations, or automated decisions where the user needs to make a choice based on the system's certainty.
UX_TMP_PPLE_HIL_001.when_not_to_apply: In domains where users expect and rely on exact statistical or numerical information (e.g., weather forecasts, sports stats, polling numbers, scientific data).
UX_TMP_PPLE_HIL_001.quote: Whenever possible, help people make decisions by conveying confidence in terms of actionable suggestions... displaying percentages or other numerical confidence values would be less valuable than providing actionable suggestions like 'This is a good time to buy'

UX_TMP_PPLE_HIL_002.title: Use Objective Language for ML Attributions
UX_TMP_PPLE_HIL_002.rule: Frame machine learning attributions (explanations for why a result is shown) using factual, action-based language rather than assuming the user's emotional state, preferences, or beliefs.
UX_TMP_PPLE_HIL_002.detect: Look for recommendation explanations using emotional or presumptuous verbs (e.g., 'Because you love...', 'Since you hate...') instead of factual action verbs (e.g., 'Because you watched...', 'Since you read...').
UX_TMP_PPLE_HIL_002.when_to_apply: When designing transparency features that explain why an algorithmic recommendation, personalized content, or proactive suggestion was made.
UX_TMP_PPLE_HIL_002.when_not_to_apply: When the user has explicitly and manually labeled a category with an emotional tag (e.g., a custom 'Things I Love' folder), though action-based framing remains generally safer.
UX_TMP_PPLE_HIL_002.quote: Keep attributions factual and based on objective analysis... Don’t provide an attribution that implies understanding or judgment of people’s emotions, preferences, or beliefs.

UX_TMP_NG_GENAI_001.title: Balance GenUI Customization with Spatial Consistency
UX_TMP_NG_GENAI_001.rule: Establish fixed design standards and persistent structural anchors in Generative UI (GenUI) systems to prevent the usability degradation and user frustration caused by constantly shifting interfaces.
UX_TMP_NG_GENAI_001.detect: Evaluate GenUI systems across multiple sessions to see if core navigation, layout structures, or primary actions unpredictably shift position or appearance based on AI generation.
UX_TMP_NG_GENAI_001.when_to_apply: When designing agentic or AI-driven systems that dynamically generate, reorder, or alter the user interface based on user context, preferences, or intent.
UX_TMP_NG_GENAI_001.when_not_to_apply: When the interface is a pure conversational stream where spatial memory of controls is irrelevant, or for single-use, ephemeral micro-tools.
UX_TMP_NG_GENAI_001.quote: As Gen UI alters the interface based on your needs, you could be shown a different UI every time you use a website. This constant relearning of the interface might cause frustration... Designers will need to figure out how to balance the gains from a completely customized experience with the losses incurred by the lack of UI consistency and predictability.

UX_TMP_NG_LOGIN_001.title: Provide a 'Show Password' Toggle for Login
UX_TMP_NG_LOGIN_001.rule: Mask passwords by default during login, but provide a user-controlled 'Show password' toggle (e.g., a checkbox or icon) to unmask the characters for error checking.
UX_TMP_NG_LOGIN_001.detect: Identify login forms with an input[type="password"]. Verify there is an associated interactive element (button/checkbox) that toggles the input type between 'password' and 'text'.
UX_TMP_NG_LOGIN_001.when_to_apply: Apply to all login interfaces, especially on mobile devices where typing complex characters is slower and more error-prone.
UX_TMP_NG_LOGIN_001.when_not_to_apply: Rarely inapplicable, though strict compliance in highly sensitive physical environments (e.g., banking terminals) might prohibit unmasking to prevent shoulder-surfing.
UX_TMP_NG_LOGIN_001.quote: Offer the option of showing passwords in clear. [...] we recommend masking the password by default and presenting users with a Show password checkbox that allows them to unmask it.

UX_TMP_H_LABELS_001.title: Provide Explicit Labels and Instructions for Login Inputs
UX_TMP_H_LABELS_001.rule: Always provide clear, visible labels or instructions for authentication form inputs (e.g., username, password, MFA) so users know exactly what data is expected and in what format.
UX_TMP_H_LABELS_001.detect: Inspect login and registration forms to ensure every data entry `<input>` has a visually apparent and programmatically associated `<label>`, and that any specific formatting rules or required field indicators are explicitly stated.
UX_TMP_H_LABELS_001.when_to_apply: When designing data entry fields for authentication flows, including login, registration, and account recovery.
UX_TMP_H_LABELS_001.when_not_to_apply: When building interactive controls not associated with data entry, such as links, buttons, or expand/collapse widgets.
UX_TMP_H_LABELS_001.quote: The intent of this Success Criterion is to have content authors present instructions or labels that identify the controls in a form so that users know what input data is expected.

UX_TMP__CAPTCHA_001.title: Programmatically Associate Form Instructions
UX_TMP__CAPTCHA_001.rule: Use `aria-describedby` to link specific field instructions (such as password requirements) to their corresponding form controls, preventing screen readers from skipping plain text between inputs during Tab navigation.
UX_TMP__CAPTCHA_001.detect: Identify form controls with adjacent instructional text. Check if the input element has an `aria-describedby` attribute referencing the ID of the instructional text element.
UX_TMP__CAPTCHA_001.when_to_apply: When providing field-specific instructions, hints, or formatting requirements (e.g., password rules in auth forms) that sit outside the primary `<label>`.
UX_TMP__CAPTCHA_001.when_not_to_apply: When instructions apply to the entire form (these should be placed at the beginning of the form) or when the primary label is fully self-explanatory.
UX_TMP__CAPTCHA_001.quote: Although labels are announced when form inputs received keyboard focus, other text between the form controls is usually skipped. Be sure to include any instructions at the beginning of the form, or associate them with specific fields using aria-describedby.

UX_TMP_RD_LISTS_001.title: Show Number of User Ratings in List Items
UX_TMP_RD_LISTS_001.rule: Always display the total number of user ratings alongside the average rating score within product list items.
UX_TMP_RD_LISTS_001.detect: Identify product list items displaying a rating average (e.g., stars). Verify that the total count of user ratings is explicitly shown next to the average.
UX_TMP_RD_LISTS_001.when_to_apply: Apply to all e-commerce product lists (category pages, search results, recommendations) where user ratings are supported and exist for the product.
UX_TMP_RD_LISTS_001.when_not_to_apply: Do not apply if the site does not feature user reviews, or if the product has no reviews (depending on the design choice to hide empty ratings).
UX_TMP_RD_LISTS_001.quote: Always Show the Number of User Ratings in List Items (5% Don’t)

UX_TMP_G_SEARCH_001.title: Make Search Prominently Visible
UX_TMP_G_SEARCH_001.rule: Display the search input field as an open, visible text box rather than hiding it behind an icon or menu to maximize discoverability.
UX_TMP_G_SEARCH_001.detect: Identify the search component in the UI. Verify that the text input field is visible by default without requiring a user interaction (like clicking a magnifying glass icon) to expand or reveal it.
UX_TMP_G_SEARCH_001.when_to_apply: When search is a primary navigation method for users, such as in e-commerce catalogs, large content repositories, or complex applications.
UX_TMP_G_SEARCH_001.when_not_to_apply: During focused conversion flows (like checkout) where global search might distract the user and lead to abandonment, unless the search is specifically scoped to the task (e.g., searching for a store location or applying a promo code).

UX_TMP_E_DESIGN_001.title: Feature at Least 40% of Product Categories on Homepage
UX_TMP_E_DESIGN_001.rule: Visually feature a broad range of product types—at least 40% of the site's top-level categories—directly on the homepage using images, thumbnails, or text links.
UX_TMP_E_DESIGN_001.detect: Calculate the percentage of top-level product categories visually represented on the homepage. Flag if it is below 40%.
UX_TMP_E_DESIGN_001.when_to_apply: When designing the homepage for an e-commerce site with a diverse or multi-category product catalog.
UX_TMP_E_DESIGN_001.when_not_to_apply: When designing for single-product stores or highly specialized brands with a very narrow product range.
UX_TMP_E_DESIGN_001.quote: Sites that sell a broad range of items should highlight a sufficiently broad range of product types (at least 40% of product types) on the homepage.

UX_TMP_LLER_NNG_001.title: Chunking Menu Items (7±2)
UX_TMP_LLER_NNG_001.rule: Group menu items into chunks of 5 to 9 (7±2) to respect working memory limits and reduce cognitive load.
UX_TMP_LLER_NNG_001.detect: Check menu lists and navigation groups. Flag any flat list of options that exceeds 9 items without visual grouping or sub-categorization.
UX_TMP_LLER_NNG_001.when_to_apply: When designing navigation menus, toolbars, or feature lists where users must scan, compare, and hold options in working memory.
UX_TMP_LLER_NNG_001.when_not_to_apply: When presenting long, naturally ordered lists (like A-Z indexes or country dropdowns) where users rely on recognition and visual scanning rather than working memory.

UX_TMP_R_MEDIUM_001.title: Conservation of Complexity (Tesler's Law)
UX_TMP_R_MEDIUM_001.rule: Shift inherent system complexity away from the user interface and into the backend system by automating tasks, providing smart defaults, and minimizing required inputs.
UX_TMP_R_MEDIUM_001.detect: Identify user flows requiring repetitive manual input, complex configuration, or multi-step processes that the system could otherwise infer, format, or automate.
UX_TMP_R_MEDIUM_001.when_to_apply: Apply to core user journeys, forms, and repetitive tasks where the system has sufficient data or context to handle the complexity internally without user intervention.
UX_TMP_R_MEDIUM_001.when_not_to_apply: Do not apply when users require granular control, when over-simplification obscures critical system behavior, or in expert interfaces where flexibility is paramount.
UX_TMP_R_MEDIUM_001.quote: UX designers need to determine whether system complexity needs to be managed internally or released to users for handling.

UX_TMP_N_TOKENS_001.title: Design Tokens as Single Source of Truth
UX_TMP_N_TOKENS_001.rule: Use design tokens as the single source of truth to name and store design decisions, ensuring consistency across design tools and codebases.
UX_TMP_N_TOKENS_001.detect: Look for hardcoded style values (e.g., hex colors, pixel spacing) in CSS or components instead of semantic token variables.
UX_TMP_N_TOKENS_001.when_to_apply: When building scalable product UIs, implementing theming (like dark mode), or maintaining a unified design system across multiple platforms.
UX_TMP_N_TOKENS_001.when_not_to_apply: When building isolated, one-off prototypes or standalone marketing pages where the overhead of a token system outweighs the benefits.
UX_TMP_N_TOKENS_001.quote: Design tokens are the single source of truth to name and store design decisions.

UX_TMP_AL_COLOR_001.title: Use Semantic Color Roles for Design Tokens
UX_TMP_AL_COLOR_001.rule: Assign colors to UI elements using semantic color roles based on emphasis, container type, and element relationships, rather than hardcoded values or generic palette names.
UX_TMP_AL_COLOR_001.detect: Check component styles for hardcoded hex values or generic palette tokens (e.g., `color: $blue-500`) instead of semantic role tokens (e.g., `color: var(--color-on-primary-container)`).
UX_TMP_AL_COLOR_001.when_to_apply: When building scalable design systems or applications that require dynamic theming (e.g., light/dark mode, user-generated themes) and guaranteed accessible contrast ratios.
UX_TMP_AL_COLOR_001.when_not_to_apply: When styling static brand assets (like logos) or specific elements where colors must remain absolutely fixed regardless of the environment or theme.
UX_TMP_AL_COLOR_001.quote: Color roles are assigned to UI elements based on emphasis, container type, and relationship with other elements. This ensures proper contrast and usage in any color scheme.

UX_TMP_KEYBOARD_001.title: Explicit Selection for High-Latency Focus Targets
UX_TMP_KEYBOARD_001.rule: Require explicit user activation (e.g., Enter or Space) to select an item if the selection triggers a network request or page refresh; do not use "selection follows focus" in these cases.
UX_TMP_KEYBOARD_001.detect: Check if arrow-key navigation in a composite widget (like a tablist or listbox) automatically triggers network requests or page reloads before the user explicitly selects the item.
UX_TMP_KEYBOARD_001.when_to_apply: When designing composite widgets (tablists, single-select listboxes) where selecting an item loads new data from the network or causes a page refresh.
UX_TMP_KEYBOARD_001.when_not_to_apply: When the content for all panels or options is already present in the DOM and displaying it is nearly instantaneous.
UX_TMP_KEYBOARD_001.quote: if displaying a new panel causes a network request and possibly a page refresh, the effect of having selection automatically focus can be devastating to the experience for keyboard and screen reader users.

UX_TMP_KEYBOARD_002.title: Distinct Visual Feedback for Focus and Selection
UX_TMP_KEYBOARD_002.rule: Provide visually distinct indicators for the keyboard focus state and the selected state, ensuring the focus indicator remains visible even when navigating among selected and unselected elements.
UX_TMP_KEYBOARD_002.detect: Observe a multi-select listbox or tablist. Verify that when an item is selected, moving the keyboard focus to another item clearly shows both the persistent selected state on the first item and the active focus indicator on the new item.
UX_TMP_KEYBOARD_002.when_to_apply: When designing widgets that support both focus navigation and selection operations (e.g., listboxes, trees, tablists).
UX_TMP_KEYBOARD_002.when_not_to_apply: Standard links or buttons where activation is instantaneous and there is no persistent "selected" state distinct from focus/active states.
UX_TMP_KEYBOARD_002.quote: The visual focus indicator must always be visible. The selected state must be visually distinct from the focus indicator.

UX_TMP_G_DIALOG_001.title: Modal Dialog Focus Trap and Keyboard Navigation
UX_TMP_G_DIALOG_001.rule: Modal dialogs must trap keyboard focus so that Tab and Shift+Tab cycle through the dialog's focusable elements without escaping to the background, and must close when the Escape key is pressed.
UX_TMP_G_DIALOG_001.detect: Open the modal. Press Tab until reaching the last focusable element; the next Tab must move focus to the first element. Press Shift+Tab on the first element; focus must move to the last. Press Escape; the modal must close.
UX_TMP_G_DIALOG_001.when_to_apply: When implementing a modal dialog that makes the rest of the page inert and requires user attention or interaction before continuing.
UX_TMP_G_DIALOG_001.when_not_to_apply: When implementing non-modal dialogs (modeless windows) where users are expected to interact with the background page simultaneously.
UX_TMP_G_DIALOG_001.quote: Tab and Shift + Tab do not move focus outside the dialog. ... If focus is on the last tabbable element inside the dialog, moves focus to the first tabbable element inside the dialog.

UX_TMP__TOOLTIP_001.title: Tooltips Must Not Contain Focusable Elements
UX_TMP__TOOLTIP_001.rule: Do not place interactive or focusable elements inside a tooltip. Because tooltip widgets do not receive focus, any interactive content within them will be inaccessible to keyboard users. Use a non-modal dialog instead for hover/focus content that requires interaction.
UX_TMP__TOOLTIP_001.detect: Query DOM for elements with role="tooltip" that contain focusable descendants (e.g., <button>, <a>, <input>, or tabindex="0").
UX_TMP__TOOLTIP_001.when_to_apply: When implementing hover or focus-triggered popups for supplementary information.
UX_TMP__TOOLTIP_001.when_not_to_apply: When implementing complex interactive popovers, which should be built as non-modal dialogs rather than tooltips.
UX_TMP__TOOLTIP_001.quote: Tooltip widgets do not receive focus. A hover that contains focusable elements can be made using a non-modal dialog.

UX_TMP_FEEDBACK_001.title: Omit Warnings for Expected Data Loss
UX_TMP_FEEDBACK_001.rule: Do not use warning alerts when data loss is the explicit and expected result of a user's action. Reserve disruptive warnings only for unexpected and irreversible data loss.
UX_TMP_FEEDBACK_001.detect: Identify confirmation modals or alerts triggered by standard 'Delete' or 'Trash' actions where the consequence is obvious and expected.
UX_TMP_FEEDBACK_001.when_to_apply: When implementing standard destructive actions where the user's intent is clear and the outcome is standard (e.g., moving a file to a recoverable trash state).
UX_TMP_FEEDBACK_001.when_not_to_apply: When the deletion has cascading, non-obvious effects, or when the action bypasses a recoverable state (e.g., permanent deletion without a trash bin).
UX_TMP_FEEDBACK_001.quote: Warn people when they initiate a task that can cause data loss that’s unexpected and irreversible. In contrast, don’t warn people when data loss is the expected result of their action.

UX_TMP_G_STATUS_001.title: Programmatically Identify Non-Focus Status Messages
UX_TMP_G_STATUS_001.rule: Use appropriate ARIA roles (e.g., role="status", role="alert") for status messages that update dynamically without stealing focus, ensuring assistive technologies can announce them.
UX_TMP_G_STATUS_001.detect: Identify dynamic text updates (e.g., 'Saved', '5 results') injected into the DOM without moving focus. Verify these elements have role='status', role='alert', or aria-live attributes.
UX_TMP_G_STATUS_001.when_to_apply: When providing feedback on the success/results of an action, waiting states, progress, or errors, and the new content is added without changing the user's context (i.e., without moving keyboard focus).
UX_TMP_G_STATUS_001.when_not_to_apply: When the feedback is presented in a modal dialog that intentionally takes focus, or when standard UI components (like accordions or tabs) simply expose/hide content.
UX_TMP_G_STATUS_001.quote: In content implemented using markup languages, status messages can be programmatically determined through role or properties such that they can be presented to the user by assistive technologies without receiving focus.

UX_TMP_NNG_UNDO_001.title: Prefer Undo Over Confirmation Dialogs
UX_TMP_NNG_UNDO_001.rule: Provide an 'Undo' option for reversible actions instead of interrupting the user with confirmation dialogs, which cause friction and lead to automatic dismissal (confirm spam).
UX_TMP_NNG_UNDO_001.detect: Identify confirmation modals triggered on frequent, reversible actions. Check if a non-blocking notification (e.g., toast) with an 'Undo' action can replace the blocking dialog.
UX_TMP_NNG_UNDO_001.when_to_apply: Apply to frequent, easily reversible actions like deleting an item, archiving, or moving files where the cost of a mistake is low.
UX_TMP_NNG_UNDO_001.when_not_to_apply: Do not apply to permanently destructive actions, actions with severe security implications, or actions that cannot be technically reversed (e.g., deleting an entire account, transferring funds).

UX_TMP_AN_STORY_001.title: Offer Informative Feedback
UX_TMP_AN_STORY_001.rule: Provide informative feedback for every user action, scaling the response magnitude to the action's frequency and importance.
UX_TMP_AN_STORY_001.detect: Check if UI elements provide visual or textual confirmation upon interaction, ensuring minor actions have subtle feedback and major actions have prominent feedback.
UX_TMP_AN_STORY_001.when_to_apply: Apply to all interactive elements where a user initiates an action, especially when the system state changes or processing takes time.
UX_TMP_AN_STORY_001.when_not_to_apply: Avoid overly intrusive or blocking feedback (like modal popups) for frequent, minor, or continuous actions.
UX_TMP_AN_STORY_001.quote: Frequent and minor actions deserve a moderate response, and infrequent and major actions should inform and answer users' typical informational, functional, and emotional needs.

UX_TMP_AN_STORY_002.title: Offer Simple Error Handling
UX_TMP_AN_STORY_002.rule: Provide clear, non-technical, and actionable error messages that help users fix specific problems without forcing them to re-enter valid data.
UX_TMP_AN_STORY_002.detect: Trigger an error state (e.g., form validation failure) and verify if the message is in plain language, highlights the specific issue, and preserves previously entered valid data.
UX_TMP_AN_STORY_002.when_to_apply: Apply to all user inputs, form submissions, and system failures where user intervention is required to proceed.
UX_TMP_AN_STORY_002.when_not_to_apply: Avoid exposing raw technical logs or stack traces to end-users under any circumstances.
UX_TMP_AN_STORY_002.quote: The information about the error shouldn't be technical. Instead, it should be expressed with accessible language... If the user incorrectly entered their phone number into a form and the rest of the data is correct, they shouldn't have to enter them again.

UX_COG_PEAKENDRULE_001.title: Aesthetic Peak-End Optimization
UX_COG_PEAKENDRULE_001.rule: Concentrate high-fidelity aesthetic polish on the most intense point of the user journey (the peak) and the final step (the end) to disproportionately improve the overall perception of the experience.
UX_COG_PEAKENDRULE_001.detect: Aesthetic effort is spread evenly across all screens, or the final confirmation/success screens are treated as an afterthought with generic styling.
UX_COG_PEAKENDRULE_001.when_to_apply: When prioritizing design resources across a complex user flow, such as a checkout process, onboarding sequence, or long-form data entry.
UX_COG_PEAKENDRULE_001.when_not_to_apply: When the entire flow is extremely short (e.g., a single-click action) where the whole interaction is essentially the peak and end simultaneously.
UX_COG_PEAKENDRULE_001.quote: By creating visually appealing highlights (a delightful animation, a beautiful confirmation screen) and ensuring the final step is seamless, you can leave a lasting positive impression that overshadows any minor frustrations.

UX_AGT_SPATIALCONSI_001.title: Balance GenUI Customization with Spatial Consistency
UX_AGT_SPATIALCONSI_001.rule: Establish fixed design standards and persistent structural anchors in Generative UI (GenUI) systems to prevent the usability degradation and user frustration caused by constantly shifting interfaces.
UX_AGT_SPATIALCONSI_001.detect: Evaluate GenUI systems across multiple sessions to see if core navigation, layout structures, or primary actions unpredictably shift position or appearance based on AI generation.
UX_AGT_SPATIALCONSI_001.when_to_apply: When designing agentic or AI-driven systems that dynamically generate, reorder, or alter the user interface based on user context, preferences, or intent.
UX_AGT_SPATIALCONSI_001.when_not_to_apply: When the interface is a pure conversational stream where spatial memory of controls is irrelevant, or for single-use, ephemeral micro-tools.
UX_AGT_SPATIALCONSI_001.quote: As Gen UI alters the interface based on your needs, you could be shown a different UI every time you use a website. This constant relearning of the interface might cause frustration... Designers will need to figure out how to balance the gains from a completely customized experience with the losses incurred by the lack of UI consistency and predictability.

UX_AGT_ACTIONABLESY_001.title: Translate ML Confidence into Actionable Suggestions
UX_AGT_ACTIONABLESY_001.rule: Present machine learning confidence scores as actionable advice or semantic categories rather than raw numerical percentages, unless the domain specifically requires statistical data.
UX_AGT_ACTIONABLESY_001.detect: Look for UI elements displaying raw ML probability percentages (e.g., '97% match', '80% confidence') outside of strictly statistical or scientific contexts.
UX_AGT_ACTIONABLESY_001.when_to_apply: When presenting predictive results, recommendations, or automated decisions where the user needs to make a choice based on the system's certainty.
UX_AGT_ACTIONABLESY_001.when_not_to_apply: In domains where users expect and rely on exact statistical or numerical information (e.g., weather forecasts, sports stats, polling numbers, scientific data).
UX_AGT_ACTIONABLESY_001.quote: Whenever possible, help people make decisions by conveying confidence in terms of actionable suggestions... displaying percentages or other numerical confidence values would be less valuable than providing actionable suggestions like 'This is a good time to buy'

UX_AGT_OBJECTIVESYS_001.title: Use Objective Language for ML Attributions
UX_AGT_OBJECTIVESYS_001.rule: Frame machine learning attributions (explanations for why a result is shown) using factual, action-based language rather than assuming the user's emotional state, preferences, or beliefs.
UX_AGT_OBJECTIVESYS_001.detect: Look for recommendation explanations using emotional or presumptuous verbs (e.g., 'Because you love...', 'Since you hate...') instead of factual action verbs (e.g., 'Because you watched...', 'Since you read...').
UX_AGT_OBJECTIVESYS_001.when_to_apply: When designing transparency features that explain why an algorithmic recommendation, personalized content, or proactive suggestion was made.
UX_AGT_OBJECTIVESYS_001.when_not_to_apply: When the user has explicitly and manually labeled a category with an emotional tag (e.g., a custom 'Things I Love' folder), though action-based framing remains generally safer.
UX_AGT_OBJECTIVESYS_001.quote: Keep attributions factual and based on objective analysis... Don’t provide an attribution that implies understanding or judgment of people’s emotions, preferences, or beliefs.

UX_GEN_PROGRAMMATIC_001.title: Programmatically Associate Form Instructions
UX_GEN_PROGRAMMATIC_001.rule: Use `aria-describedby` to link specific field instructions (such as password requirements) to their corresponding form controls, preventing screen readers from skipping plain text between inputs during Tab navigation.
UX_GEN_PROGRAMMATIC_001.detect: Identify form controls with adjacent instructional text. Check if the input element has an `aria-describedby` attribute referencing the ID of the instructional text element.
UX_GEN_PROGRAMMATIC_001.when_to_apply: When providing field-specific instructions, hints, or formatting requirements (e.g., password rules in auth forms) that sit outside the primary `<label>`.
UX_GEN_PROGRAMMATIC_001.when_not_to_apply: When instructions apply to the entire form (these should be placed at the beginning of the form) or when the primary label is fully self-explanatory.
UX_GEN_PROGRAMMATIC_001.quote: Although labels are announced when form inputs received keyboard focus, other text between the form controls is usually skipped. Be sure to include any instructions at the beginning of the form, or associate them with specific fields using aria-describedby.

UX_GEN_VISIBLEFORML_001.title: Provide Explicit Labels and Instructions for Login Inputs
UX_GEN_VISIBLEFORML_001.rule: Always provide clear, visible labels or instructions for authentication form inputs (e.g., username, password, MFA) so users know exactly what data is expected and in what format.
UX_GEN_VISIBLEFORML_001.detect: Inspect login and registration forms to ensure every data entry `<input>` has a visually apparent and programmatically associated `<label>`, and that any specific formatting rules or required field indicators are explicitly stated.
UX_GEN_VISIBLEFORML_001.when_to_apply: When designing data entry fields for authentication flows, including login, registration, and account recovery.
UX_GEN_VISIBLEFORML_001.when_not_to_apply: When building interactive controls not associated with data entry, such as links, buttons, or expand/collapse widgets.
UX_GEN_VISIBLEFORML_001.quote: The intent of this Success Criterion is to have content authors present instructions or labels that identify the controls in a form so that users know what input data is expected.

UX_PRD_HOMEPAGECATE_001.title: Feature at Least 40% of Product Categories on Homepage
UX_PRD_HOMEPAGECATE_001.rule: Visually feature a broad range of product types—at least 40% of the site's top-level categories—directly on the homepage using images, thumbnails, or text links.
UX_PRD_HOMEPAGECATE_001.detect: Calculate the percentage of top-level product categories visually represented on the homepage. Flag if it is below 40%.
UX_PRD_HOMEPAGECATE_001.when_to_apply: When designing the homepage for an e-commerce site with a diverse or multi-category product catalog.
UX_PRD_HOMEPAGECATE_001.when_not_to_apply: When designing for single-product stores or highly specialized brands with a very narrow product range.
UX_PRD_HOMEPAGECATE_001.quote: Sites that sell a broad range of items should highlight a sufficiently broad range of product types (at least 40% of product types) on the homepage.

UX_PRD_SEARCHDISCOV_001.title: Make Search Prominently Visible
UX_PRD_SEARCHDISCOV_001.rule: Display the search input field as an open, visible text box rather than hiding it behind an icon or menu to maximize discoverability.
UX_PRD_SEARCHDISCOV_001.detect: Identify the search component in the UI. Verify that the text input field is visible by default without requiring a user interaction (like clicking a magnifying glass icon) to expand or reveal it.
UX_PRD_SEARCHDISCOV_001.when_to_apply: When search is a primary navigation method for users, such as in e-commerce catalogs, large content repositories, or complex applications.
UX_PRD_SEARCHDISCOV_001.when_not_to_apply: During focused conversion flows (like checkout) where global search might distract the user and lead to abandonment, unless the search is specifically scoped to the task (e.g., searching for a store location or applying a promo code).

UX_PRD_SOCIALPROOFV_001.title: Show Number of User Ratings in List Items
UX_PRD_SOCIALPROOFV_001.rule: Always display the total number of user ratings alongside the average rating score within product list items.
UX_PRD_SOCIALPROOFV_001.detect: Identify product list items displaying a rating average (e.g., stars). Verify that the total count of user ratings is explicitly shown next to the average.
UX_PRD_SOCIALPROOFV_001.when_to_apply: Apply to all e-commerce product lists (category pages, search results, recommendations) where user ratings are supported and exist for the product.
UX_PRD_SOCIALPROOFV_001.when_not_to_apply: Do not apply if the site does not feature user reviews, or if the product has no reviews (depending on the design choice to hide empty ratings).
UX_PRD_SOCIALPROOFV_001.quote: Always Show the Number of User Ratings in List Items (5% Don’t)

UX_COG_MILLERSLAW_002.title: Chunking Menu Items (7±2)
UX_COG_MILLERSLAW_002.rule: Group menu items into chunks of 5 to 9 (7±2) to respect working memory limits and reduce cognitive load.
UX_COG_MILLERSLAW_002.detect: Check menu lists and navigation groups. Flag any flat list of options that exceeds 9 items without visual grouping or sub-categorization.
UX_COG_MILLERSLAW_002.when_to_apply: When designing navigation menus, toolbars, or feature lists where users must scan, compare, and hold options in working memory.
UX_COG_MILLERSLAW_002.when_not_to_apply: When presenting long, naturally ordered lists (like A-Z indexes or country dropdowns) where users rely on recognition and visual scanning rather than working memory.

UX_DS_SINGLESOURCE_001.title: Design Tokens as Single Source of Truth
UX_DS_SINGLESOURCE_001.rule: Use design tokens as the single source of truth to name and store design decisions, ensuring consistency across design tools and codebases.
UX_DS_SINGLESOURCE_001.detect: Look for hardcoded style values (e.g., hex colors, pixel spacing) in CSS or components instead of semantic token variables.
UX_DS_SINGLESOURCE_001.when_to_apply: When building scalable product UIs, implementing theming (like dark mode), or maintaining a unified design system across multiple platforms.
UX_DS_SINGLESOURCE_001.when_not_to_apply: When building isolated, one-off prototypes or standalone marketing pages where the overhead of a token system outweighs the benefits.
UX_DS_SINGLESOURCE_001.quote: Design tokens are the single source of truth to name and store design decisions.

UX_DS_SEMANTICTOKE_001.title: Use Semantic Color Roles for Design Tokens
UX_DS_SEMANTICTOKE_001.rule: Assign colors to UI elements using semantic color roles based on emphasis, container type, and element relationships, rather than hardcoded values or generic palette names.
UX_DS_SEMANTICTOKE_001.detect: Check component styles for hardcoded hex values or generic palette tokens (e.g., `color: $blue-500`) instead of semantic role tokens (e.g., `color: var(--color-on-primary-container)`).
UX_DS_SEMANTICTOKE_001.when_to_apply: When building scalable design systems or applications that require dynamic theming (e.g., light/dark mode, user-generated themes) and guaranteed accessible contrast ratios.
UX_DS_SEMANTICTOKE_001.when_not_to_apply: When styling static brand assets (like logos) or specific elements where colors must remain absolutely fixed regardless of the environment or theme.
UX_DS_SEMANTICTOKE_001.quote: Color roles are assigned to UI elements based on emphasis, container type, and relationship with other elements. This ensures proper contrast and usage in any color scheme.

UX_INX_MINIMIZECONF_001.title: Prefer Undo Over Confirmation Dialogs
UX_INX_MINIMIZECONF_001.rule: Provide an 'Undo' option for reversible actions and omit warnings for expected, recoverable data loss. Reserve blocking confirmation dialogs only for unexpected, permanently destructive, or irreversible actions to prevent alert fatigue.
UX_INX_MINIMIZECONF_001.detect: Identify confirmation modals triggered by frequent, reversible actions (e.g., standard 'Delete' or 'Archive'). Check if a non-blocking notification (e.g., toast) with an 'Undo' action can replace the blocking dialog.
UX_INX_MINIMIZECONF_001.when_to_apply: When implementing frequent, easily reversible actions where the user's intent is clear, the cost of a mistake is low, and the outcome is standard (e.g., moving a file to a recoverable trash state).
UX_INX_MINIMIZECONF_001.when_not_to_apply: When an action has cascading, non-obvious effects, severe security implications, or results in unexpected and permanently irreversible data loss (e.g., deleting an entire account, transferring funds, bypassing a trash bin).
UX_INX_MINIMIZECONF_001.quote: Warn people when they initiate a task that can cause data loss that’s unexpected and irreversible. In contrast, don’t warn people when data loss is the expected result of their action.

UX_INX_MODALFOCUSTR_001.title: Modal Dialog Focus Trap and Keyboard Navigation
UX_INX_MODALFOCUSTR_001.rule: Modal dialogs must trap keyboard focus so that Tab and Shift+Tab cycle through the dialog's focusable elements without escaping to the background, and must close when the Escape key is pressed.
UX_INX_MODALFOCUSTR_001.detect: Open the modal. Press Tab until reaching the last focusable element; the next Tab must move focus to the first element. Press Shift+Tab on the first element; focus must move to the last. Press Escape; the modal must close.
UX_INX_MODALFOCUSTR_001.when_to_apply: When implementing a modal dialog that makes the rest of the page inert and requires user attention or interaction before continuing.
UX_INX_MODALFOCUSTR_001.when_not_to_apply: When implementing non-modal dialogs (modeless windows) where users are expected to interact with the background page simultaneously.
UX_INX_MODALFOCUSTR_001.quote: Tab and Shift + Tab do not move focus outside the dialog. ... If focus is on the last tabbable element inside the dialog, moves focus to the first tabbable element inside the dialog.

UX_INX_EXPLICITSELE_001.title: Explicit Selection for High-Latency Focus Targets
UX_INX_EXPLICITSELE_001.rule: Require explicit user activation (e.g., Enter or Space) to select an item if the selection triggers a network request or page refresh; do not use "selection follows focus" in these cases.
UX_INX_EXPLICITSELE_001.detect: Check if arrow-key navigation in a composite widget (like a tablist or listbox) automatically triggers network requests or page reloads before the user explicitly selects the item.
UX_INX_EXPLICITSELE_001.when_to_apply: When designing composite widgets (tablists, single-select listboxes) where selecting an item loads new data from the network or causes a page refresh.
UX_INX_EXPLICITSELE_001.when_not_to_apply: When the content for all panels or options is already present in the DOM and displaying it is nearly instantaneous.
UX_INX_EXPLICITSELE_001.quote: if displaying a new panel causes a network request and possibly a page refresh, the effect of having selection automatically focus can be devastating to the experience for keyboard and screen reader users.

UX_INX_FOCUSSELECTI_001.title: Distinct Visual Feedback for Focus and Selection
UX_INX_FOCUSSELECTI_001.rule: Provide visually distinct indicators for the keyboard focus state and the selected state, ensuring the focus indicator remains visible even when navigating among selected and unselected elements.
UX_INX_FOCUSSELECTI_001.detect: Observe a multi-select listbox or tablist. Verify that when an item is selected, moving the keyboard focus to another item clearly shows both the persistent selected state on the first item and the active focus indicator on the new item.
UX_INX_FOCUSSELECTI_001.when_to_apply: When designing widgets that support both focus navigation and selection operations (e.g., listboxes, trees, tablists).
UX_INX_FOCUSSELECTI_001.when_not_to_apply: Standard links or buttons where activation is instantaneous and there is no persistent "selected" state distinct from focus/active states.
UX_INX_FOCUSSELECTI_001.quote: The visual focus indicator must always be visible. The selected state must be visually distinct from the focus indicator.

UX_INX_INFORMATIVEF_001.title: Offer Informative Feedback
UX_INX_INFORMATIVEF_001.rule: Provide informative feedback for every user action, scaling the response magnitude to the action's frequency and importance.
UX_INX_INFORMATIVEF_001.detect: Check if UI elements provide visual or textual confirmation upon interaction, ensuring minor actions have subtle feedback and major actions have prominent feedback.
UX_INX_INFORMATIVEF_001.when_to_apply: Apply to all interactive elements where a user initiates an action, especially when the system state changes or processing takes time.
UX_INX_INFORMATIVEF_001.when_not_to_apply: Avoid overly intrusive or blocking feedback (like modal popups) for frequent, minor, or continuous actions.
UX_INX_INFORMATIVEF_001.quote: Frequent and minor actions deserve a moderate response, and infrequent and major actions should inform and answer users' typical informational, functional, and emotional needs.

UX_INX_TOOLTIPINTER_001.title: Tooltips Must Not Contain Focusable Elements
UX_INX_TOOLTIPINTER_001.rule: Do not place interactive or focusable elements inside a tooltip. Because tooltip widgets do not receive focus, any interactive content within them will be inaccessible to keyboard users. Use a non-modal dialog instead for hover/focus content that requires interaction.
UX_INX_TOOLTIPINTER_001.detect: Query DOM for elements with role="tooltip" that contain focusable descendants (e.g., <button>, <a>, <input>, or tabindex="0").
UX_INX_TOOLTIPINTER_001.when_to_apply: When implementing hover or focus-triggered popups for supplementary information.
UX_INX_TOOLTIPINTER_001.when_not_to_apply: When implementing complex interactive popovers, which should be built as non-modal dialogs rather than tooltips.
UX_INX_TOOLTIPINTER_001.quote: Tooltip widgets do not receive focus. A hover that contains focusable elements can be made using a non-modal dialog.
